digest.component_or_area: RP-04 secrets and authentication design research
propositions: Rebar must safely pass credentials through multiple environments (local, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, AWS-hosted, CLI, library, MCP) while delegating auth ownership to official SDKs, helpers, and CI platforms rather than implementing a universal secret broker.

Current Rebar defect: _bridge_runner copies full parent environment to reconciler child and ticket delivery, leaking unrelated Jira/LLM/cloud credentials; RP-04 must replace this with adapter-owned baseline plus only selected auth capability.

Recommended design uses immutable non-secret OperationSnapshot with typed injection of constructed clients and provider-specific auth objects; static credentials materialize only at the adapter that requires them, never in universal lookup or ambient fallback.

Long-running processes (MCP/server) require restart/redeploy for static-secret rotation; short-lived CLI processes receive current startup environment; native temporary/workload credentials remain SDK-owned and may refresh in-process.

Mature OSS prior art (Git, GitHub CLI, PydanticAI, Airflow, jira-cli) converge on provider/helper/runtime-owned authentication with URL-scoped helpers, explicit typed injection, and separation of non-secret config from credential material.

MCP schemas and arguments must never accept raw credentials or allow lower-trust callers to select stronger server identity; all operations instantiate only needed runtimes with explicit auth selection failing closed without ambient or anonymous fallback.
